done_when: forge work on a branch with an unfinished merge either hands the worker the conflicts to resolve and records its start without a partial commit (so the record lands with the merge commit), or, if that can't be done safely, refuses with a plain next step (resolve and commit the merge, then rerun) instead of a git error and a doctor hint; command tests cover a conflicted default-branch merge on a task and a fix, for a new repo and one adopted on an earlier release

findings.body: Raise: Not done. The previously reported configuration-conflict gap remains for both task and fix checkouts. When branch settings and a default-branch update conflict in `forge.toml`, running `forge work` from the item's checkout reaches `src/forge/cli.py:138` first. That calls `check_pin`, which parses the caller's configuration at `src/forge/repo.py:578`; conflict markers trigger the refusal at line 456 with `Next: forge doctor` (line 36). The new merge guard is never reached, so the required resolve-and-commit guidance is absent. The four passing command cases conflict only in `merge.txt` (`tests/test_work_requires_a_finished_merge.py:64–75`) and cannot catch this failure. Check the target's pending merge before caller configuration parsing and cover this command path.
findings.title: Not done: unfinished merges with a conflicted forge.toml still produce a doctor hint

why: forge work fails before the worker starts on a branch with a merge in progress ('git commit failed: fatal: cannot do a partial commit during a merge. Next: forge doctor'), because its 'is working' record is a partial commit; this traps branches whose default-branch merge left conflicts for a worker to resolve (reported by a client session on v1.2.8)
